sections.title: Focused inpaint is a frontend crop+enlarge — not a missing V5 model
sections.lede: Community thought V5 lacked Focused inpaint. Staff: it crops the mask in the UI, then calls whatever inpaint model you already have.
sections.body:
Community spent part of the window sure V5 had lost Focused inpaint. The UI receipt (Ryoooshu screenshot in this issue) and staff prose say otherwise: Focused inpaint is not a separate V5 model feature you wait for — it is a **frontend** crop-and-enlarge of the masked region, then a normal call into whichever inpainting model you already selected. ght901: it is supported **automatically on any inpainting model**. That kills the "V5 lacks Focused" rumor without inventing a new sampler or PE() contract.

Usage still matters. Free Focused inpaint **drains Opus usage** the same way other free gens do. Paid Anlas paths generally skip the Opus usage meter — the standing Anlas≠usage STAFF rule from Wednesday — with the known exception that multi-image gens inside the free window still charge usage on the first unpaid frame. Do not confuse Focused inpaint with Focused Area Selection / Minimum Context Area 32 (the older V5→V4.5 tiny-patch anecdote). One is a frontend enlarge before inpaint; the other is a context-area knob for small cross-model patches.

Practical read: if your V5 Full inpaint looks soft on a tiny facial fix, try Focused inpaint before you blame the model or invent a strength recipe. Log the Opus tick when free so Studio meter copy stays honest.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, inpaint on a small facial tweak. A: normal inpaint mask. B: Focused inpaint on the same mask. Log whether B looks sharper on the patch and whether Opus usage ticks on both when free. Optional C: paid Enhance/Anlas path — confirm usage meter stays flat while Anlas moves.

**CTA.** Guren: one A/B in Laboratory only (Opus/free). Ivory: Studio copy should say frontend crop+enlarge, not "V5 missing Focused." Chiyo: board only if product chrome still implies V5 lacks it.

sections.title: eyes visible through hair means translucent bangs — avoid it for a solid peek
sections.lede: That tag is not a soft bang peek. Staff: it is specifically the see-through hair-over-eye look.
sections.body:
Bangs-over-eye is one of those tags people treat as a soft peek when it is actually a specific optical effect. Noka framed the fork cleanly: either hair completely covers an eye, or bangs sit over an eye visible *through* the hair as if the strands were see-through. ght901 locked the mechanism on advice — if you are using `eyes visible through hair`, that translucent hair effect is **specifically** what the tag is for.

So the HOUSE/Studio footgun is clear: do not paste the tag when you want a solid bang with only a partial iris peek. Drop it and steer with ordinary bang / hair-over-one-eye language instead. This window did **not** land a reliable translucent-free peek recipe — that stays an open question in ANALYSIS. Same-seed A/B is the only honest next step: one roll with the tag, one without, identical everything else.

Keep the prompt lowercase per HOUSE. Do not invent a weight stack around the tag; staff did not give one.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler/karras, guidance 5, 28 steps, QT on. Base: `1girl, bangs, one eye covered`. A: add `eyes visible through hair`. B: omit that tag; keep `bangs over eyes` / `hair over one eye` only. Compare translucent see-through vs solid cover/peek.

**CTA.** Guren: one same-seed A/B in Laboratory. Ivory: Studio tip cards should not sell the tag as a generic bang-peek. Open: translucent-free peek remains unsolved.

sections.title: | split ≈ character prompts without a position — AI chooses
sections.lede: Staff yes'd the equivalence. Community caveat: V5 may not byte-match | vs boxes the way v4.x did.
sections.body:
Character-prompt UX and the old `|` splitter keep colliding in advice threads. Ryoooshu asked the precise question: is using `|` to split multiple characters the same as the character-prompt feature **without** specifying a position (letting the AI decide)? ght901 answered with a flat yes. That is the STAFF land for this Friday — `|` ≈ unpositioned character prompts; the model chooses placement.

Two guardrails stay. First: never mix `|` character syntax with character boxes — that remains OFFICIAL-DOCS / standing Don't. Second: Uchariko's companion anecdote — on V5, swapping `|` for boxes may **not** byte-match the same image the way v4.x often did. Practically the split still works; bit-identical restores across the two UIs are not a promise. Label the byte-match caveat `[ANECDOTE]` / `[UNOFFICIAL]` until staff says otherwise.

When you need per-character UC or pinned positions, prefer boxes. When you only need a fast multi-char split and can accept AI placement, `|` is staff-endorsed as equivalent to empty-position boxes.

**Try this.** Same seed family, V5 Full, Euler/karras, guidance 5, 28 steps, QT on, two characters. A: base scene + `|` split identities (no positions). B: same identities as character boxes with positions empty / AI choice. C optional: boxes with explicit positions. Compare placement stability and whether A≈B pixel-wise.

**CTA.** Guren: one A/B (Laboratory). Ivory: Studio docs may say `|` ≈ unpositioned boxes — add the V5 byte-match caveat as ANECDOTE, not STAFF.

excerpts.speaker: Uchariko

sections.title: Saved site PNGs already carry the prompt — /inspect is optional
sections.lede: luna: share the download; Discord /inspect is not required. Browser bugs can strip metadata.
sections.body:
Advice threads still ping `/inspect` out of habit. luna's UX clarification is small and useful: if you share images that still carry metadata, readers do not need Discord `/inspect` specifically to read the prompt. Images saved from the NAI website generally embed that metadata. Browser bugs can strip it sometimes — so a "empty metadata" complaint is first a re-save / browser check, not a model bug.

This is a light tip, not a new generation recipe. It pairs with the older upscaler note that from 2026-08-25 upscales also carry metadata. For Studio cohesion: a "download and share" tip can mention embedded prompts without teaching users to scrape Discord. For Guren: one keeper download verified in a metadata viewer is enough validation; no gen API required this run. For desk readers: treat a metadata-empty Discord upload as a browser/save issue first. This tip does not change generation settings, samplers, or UC.

**Try this.** Download one keeper from novelai.net. A: open in a metadata viewer / NAI import. B: re-upload to Discord without `/inspect` and confirm a reader can still see the prompt. If metadata is missing, retry the save path before blaming the model.

**CTA.** Ivory: Studio "share tip" copy can mention embedded metadata. Chiyo: only board if product wants a download-metadata chrome note.

sections.title: Precise Reference is single-character only — multi-char leaks
sections.lede: Sigurd: cannot assign PR per character box. Multi-person refs still count as one character and mix.
sections.body:
Precise Reference is still a V4.5-lane tool (not launched on V5), and Sigurd's advice reply tightens how to use it when you are on that lane. PR is **single-character only** — you cannot assign a reference per character box. Multi-character prompts plus one reference produce severe leak into every character. A reference image that itself contains multiple people still counts as one character and mixes them. Prompt vs reference contradictions override or mix rather than cleanly layering.

Mark `[UNOFFICIAL]` / `[ANECDOTE]` until STAFF or OFFICIAL-DOCS repeats it. Do not invent a multi-PR workflow or claim V5 suddenly grew PR. Recurring OC identity on V5 remains "no clean answer until PR ships" — this anecdote does not change that; it only prevents a leaky V4.5 setup from being documented as a Studio default. Studio should keep PR tips in the V4.5 exception lane and warn that one reference cannot be "assigned" across boxes. Multi-person sheet refs are still one PR slot.

**Try this.** On V4.5 Full only (PR path). Same seed. A: one character + matching single-person PR. B: two character boxes + the same single-person PR. Compare leak. Do not invent a multi-PR recipe.

**CTA.** Guren: optional one V4.5 A/B if battery allows. Ivory: do not Studio-promote multi-char PR. Keep label ANECDOTE.

excerpts.speaker: Sigurd 70B {SergalAluminum}
excerpts.text: Precise Reference is only meant to work with one character … can't be assigned to different characters. Multi-char + one reference → severe leak. Multi characters in a reference → mix.

sections.title: Chunks are text placeholders — surrounding weights apply; dangling :: kills them
sections.lede: Uchariko: chunks expand to assigned text. AmbiProp: a dangling :: inside the chunk terminates weighting.
sections.body:
Prompt Chunks look special in the editor; the model side is simpler. Uchariko: chunks are basically placeholders for the text assigned to them — they do not function all that differently from typing that text in place. AmbiProp closed the weight footgun: if a chunk body contains a dangling `::`, that terminates weighting early because the stream is read normally. Surrounding `n::…::` **does** apply to the expanded text when the closes are clean.

Practical hygiene: double-click a chunk in the prompt to inspect expansion before you chase a mystery weight. Keep chunk bodies free of stray `::` unless you intentionally want to end an emphasis block. Comma-wrap chunks when you need them to behave like a single token in a list (`painterly, [chunk], best quality`) — that older anecdote still sits next to this one in the guide. If a weighted chunk mysteriously stops mid-phrase, inspect the chunk body for an accidental `::` before raising guidance or rewriting the artist list.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full. Make a chunk whose body is `soft lighting, detailed background`. A: wrap as `1.3::[chunk]::`. B: put a dangling `::` inside the chunk body and wrap the same way. Compare whether B truncates the weight. Double-click to confirm expansion.

**CTA.** Guren: one Laboratory check. Ivory: Studio chunk help should mention weight inheritance + dangling `::`.

excerpts.speaker: Uchariko
excerpts.text: Yes, the chunks are basically just placeholders for the text assigned to them, they don't function all that differently from just typing in the text in that space

excerpts.speaker: AmbiProp
excerpts.text: So if a chunk had a dangling :: in it, that would terminate weighting as it just reads normally to the model.

sections.title: Artist dilution — try QT+UC off for western styles
sections.lede: AmbiProp: every tag shares context. More tags/weights pull away from the artist.
sections.body:
Western and other non-anime artists keep losing a fight with V5's default anime lean. AmbiProp's mechanism note is the useful bit: every tag shares context, so the more tags and weights you stack, the more you pull away from the artist's influence. The working habit they described — often turn off default quality prompts and the UC preset, reinforce with medium tags such as `oil painting (medium)` or `semi-realistic`, and A|B start weights around `0.8::artist:name::` versus `1.5::artist:name::` — is an `[UNOFFICIAL]` `[ANECDOTE]`, not CONSENSUS.

It pairs with STAFF classical/`fine art` guidance without replacing it. Classical Monet-class work still wants `fine art` and a slim or off QT; this western-style note is the broader dilution story for anyone fighting anime defaults. Same-seed ladders only. Do not auto-flip Studio QT defaults from one voice. Same-seed only; if B/C win, label the memory ANECDOTE — never promote a one-voice QT-off habit to CONSENSUS or Studio default.

**Try this.** Same seed, V5 Full, Euler/karras, guidance 5, 28 steps. Pick one western/non-anime `artist:name`. A: QT on + UC Light + bare artist. B: QT off + UC preset off + medium tag + `0.8::artist:name::`. C: same as B with `1.5::artist:name::`. Compare anime lean vs style lock.

**CTA.** Guren: one three-way in Laboratory; `save_memory` if B/C win. Ivory: do not auto-flip Studio QT defaults from one voice.

excerpts.text: every tag is sharing context so the more tags and weights, the more it pulls away from the artist's influence… often turn off default quality prompts and UC preset… start with `0.8:: artist::` and `1.5:: artist::`

## Friday Laboratory board — Guren Try-this ladder (2026-09-18)

Opus/free only in Laboratory. Battery 100%→99% (~12 gens). No Anlas spend. Public hop staticforge.737.jp.net.

### Winners
1. **eyes-visible-through-hair** — Tag = translucent bangs. For solid peek use bangs over eyes / hair over one eye only (omit the translucent tag). Same seed A/B confirmed.
2. **pipe-vs-charprompt** — Unpositioned `|` ≈ character boxes with AI position for placement stability (red-left/blonde-right both). Metadata differs: pipe stays in base_caption (`char_captions=[]`); boxes write `char_captions`. MCP does not auto-split `|` into boxes. Not byte-identical.
3. **chunks-placeholders** — No named chunk UI on `generate_image`. Weight-wrap `1.3::soft lighting, detailed background::` works. Dangling `::` inside the span closes the weight early (forge normalizes to truncated form).
4. **artist-dilution-western** — QT on + UC light + bare `artist:alphonse mucha` → anime lean. **QT off + UC 0 + art nouveau + painting (medium) + `0.8::artist:alphonse mucha::`** locks Art Nouveau/Mucha. 1.5 similar; 0.8 enough.
5. **fur-no-artist-tags** (optional) — v5 `include:[furry]` stripped by MCP. Furry model + `zero pictured` still drew an animal; `artist:zaush` did not clear-lock style. Keep zero pictured; do not recipe-hunt e621 artists.

### Skips
- focused-inpaint-frontend — no mask UI on MCP (same as Wednesday).
- precise-reference-single-char — no V4.5 PR path on MCP.
- grim Vitou/steam — off billboard.

Memory: `friday_2026_09_18_lab_board`. Local: `/workspace/lab-friday-2026-09-18/REPORT.md`.
